chapter: Train trip with the rich sponsors
title: Monroe Boost Club sign and days in New Orleans
summary: In New Orleans Love ties a man's necktie for a tip, hangs the Monroe Boost Club sign on the coach, and the band practices in the baggage car while Frankie Dusen, Peter Bocage and others visit.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I said, all right. Say, I guess you boys, we won't see y'all until the head report up at the Greenwald Hotel, used to call the roads at the Greenwald. Report every morning because they didn't know exactly when they'd leave, you see. They didn't want us to get mixed up. So, I come out on the platform and this fellow, I tell him, old man, Miles, he didn't know how to tie his necktie, you know. He wanted to tie it like this. And you see him, I'm tired, yeah. He said, can you tie that boy? I said, yeah, tie my tie for him. I tied a tie for him, you know, and look in the glass, he looked at me. He said, that's fine, that's just fine. And on his hand, his pocket, give me $5. I said, gee whee, them fellows is giving us a break. Yeah. And here come this Dr. William. He said, Ed, get one of your boys there and put this sign out. Man, it was long as the coach was, you know. And they had ropes on it, a sea grass rope. Ed tied that in on the train, I tied this in, you know. Tied tight, put a swamp knot in it, you know, so you could just pull it and get it down. It says Monroe Boost Club.
Boost, Boost, I don't know what it's called. Boost Club. Boost. Boost. Like you're boosting something.

Yeah, Boost. Monroe Boost Club. Boost. He gave me and Ed five dollars a piece to put that sign on both sides of the coach. And so he said, well, y'all get ready to go. Mr. Williams, that's the one. Dr. Williams. He said, well, y'all go into town? I said, yeah, we're going to run up town. Other boys didn't know nothing about New Orleans, but I knew, you see. Sure. He said, we're going up to Ramport Street. Well, the coaches will be there. You won't have to come back up here and call them. They'll just go down to Union Station and say, Dan Tucker will have the beer cool in the baggage car. That's why y'all have y'all fun. If you got any friends, just bring them aboard and give them some beer and let them have their fun with you. Yeah. And let them have their fun with you. And they said, well, Dr. Williams, I said, well, you all go into town? Yeah, we're going to town. Dr. Williams, I said, I'll bring it up here about this evening sometime when Ed Williams was going to see fit that we can come. You know, they want to hear our band play. Frankie Duesen and all them, Connors and Peter Bocas and all them. They're always on Ramport Street, you know. So we go down and the coaches was in. We get some bull there and started drinking, you know. And got our band in the baggage car and we start to practice. You know, that band used to practice every time they get a chance, every day. Man, we was in there practicing. You think we was playing for somebody. Yeah. Man, here come Frankie Duesen looking at him and I said, hello Frankie. Hello, you big ass so and so. Yeah. Oh, he's a nasty fella, you know. He said, look at that, look at that, Pete. Look at that little old big ass fella there. Remember Bunny in there with us on the train that day and us killed him? And after a while, here comes Joe Howard. Man, less time than about a half hour, the all was there. We got him a bull, you know, and fill him up with liquor. Cigars and everything. We ain't, oh, them old fellas used to throw some money away. And Ed had to go every day at nine o'clock find out when they left. We stayed down there four days. Oh, yeah. Doing nothing. Just practicing and playing on me.
